title: Engagement spec
description: Single source of truth for one client engagement (ADR 0002). Produced by the discovery engine from a questionnaire or chatbot interview; consumed by the deck, backlog and build agents. Unknown answers are omitted (never null) and listed in approach.risks.open_items; answer provenance lives in /provenance keyed by JSON pointer.

legal_entities.description: Legal entities that sell (one per country or region); more than one in one store needs Shopify Plus

brand_count.description: Distinct customer-facing brands this engagement needs a Shopify storefront for. Not a market fact: two brands can share one market, or one brand can span every market. Shopify's expansion-store eligibility requires each store to be an extension of the main brand with identical branding, so a genuinely separate brand needs its own store and its own Shopify Plus subscription — not one of the ten a single Plus contract includes.

consent.description: ADR 0007 — LLM processing of client answers requires recorded consent.

language.description: The language the engagement is run in, and the language every client-facing document generated from it is written in. Stamped from the interview session; absent on engagements produced before it existed.

name.description: Optional personal data — redacted before any LLM call (ADR 0007).

offer.description: Computed by the discovery engine from ai/schema/offering.json — never entered by hand.

l_triggers.description: One trigger. A headless storefront cannot be a Foundation or a Scale at any catalogue size, so it lands in Ecommerce Growth and the delivery track follows the answer. Luxury positioning was never a size and a complete Figma design system is built inside the offers (the storefront design gate, bespoke tier). Content or a front end outside Shopify is not a trigger at all — it is exit rule 11.26 and Merkle Arc. More than one Shopify store (the engine's own derived market topology, never a client answer) is the other trigger: Shopify documents no market-count cap per store, so global reach alone never forces this — only a topology that genuinely needs a second store does.

addons.description: What goes past the promise of the pack this engagement is named after, one entry per scope gate. The quote already contains them: the price is the Foundation base plus every active gate at its own weeks and price, so this names the add-ons rather than pricing them. Empty when the engagement is the pack as packaged.

units.description: How many of the gate's units the engagement takes (markets, languages, integrations, stores beyond the first, POS locations, further designs).

included_units.description: How many of those units the pack's promise already includes.

gate_capacity_weeks.description: Weeks of scope gates this pack's band spans (its duration minus the Foundation's). Shown on the pack pages and read by exit rule 11.3; the quote itself is the Foundation base plus every active gate, so this no longer moves the price.

scope_effort_weeks.description: Weeks the base offer plus the active scope gates add up to. The offer is chosen from this, not from the number of gates: a Magento migration and a 500-SKU catalogue are one gate each and differ by an order of magnitude.

scope_effort_by_gate.description: The scope effort itemised by gate, heaviest first. The total alone cannot be acted on: a scope that has outgrown the largest offer needs to say where the weeks are.

primary_markets.description: One or more markets that lead revenue and launch priority (e.g. US and EU for a global brand).

selling_entity.description: The legal entity that sells and invoices the customer in this market (a name from /meta/client/legal_entities). Business fact, not an architecture choice.

assortment.description: How this market's range relates to the primary market: identical, a subset of it, or a deliberately different range.

run_by.description: Who runs the market day to day: one central team, or a local team that sets its own prices, campaigns and content.

distinct_theme_design.description: Whether this market needs its own theme design — different theme settings (colors, typography) or Liquid templates — rather than the same theme with market-specific content. Shopify's per-market customization never reaches theme settings or templates, only section content and block visibility.

ddp_markets.description: Countries where duties and import taxes are collected at checkout (DDP); others are DAP.

tax_registration_appetite.description: Whether the business intends to hold and file its own tax registrations in destination countries, or would rather a partner be the legal seller. Business appetite, not an architecture choice.

topology.description: DERIVED by the topology evaluator (never answered): how many stores the markets run on. See ai/engine/topology.js.

source.description: Official Shopify source, when the trigger rests on a platform fact rather than business governance.
Official Shopify source, when the assumption rests on a platform fact.

separate_store_markets.description: Markets that get their own store: the diverging subset under a hybrid recommendation, or every market under a full expansion-stores recommendation.

additional_channel_stores.description: Stores a channel needs regardless of market count — today only 'B2B', when wholesale is run as its own operation. Independent of separate_store_markets; storesBeyondTheFirst() (ai/engine/classify.js) sums both.

uk_considerations.description: Present when the headquarters country is GB: UK Managed Markets has its own terms (fulfilment confined to Great Britain or Northern Ireland, no Shopify Protect, no multi-currency payouts, VAT registration must match the business name) that this evaluator cannot check from a country code alone.

per_market_theme_note.description: Present whenever the recommendation leaves more than one market on the same store: per-market theme content needs the Advanced plan or higher.

china.description: Mainland China discovery inputs (only when CN is a launch market). Not part of the Merkle offering (exit rule 11.20); see ai/docs/china-mainland.md.

customisation.description: Checkout changes in Shopify terms. Editor branding and Thank you / Order status blocks: all plans; step extensions and Checkout Branding API: Plus; a fully custom checkout UI is not possible on Shopify (11.6).

multi_address_orders.description: One order delivered to more than one address. Shopify cannot do this: split shipping divides an order into several shipments but they all go to a single address (exit rule 11.27).

fulfilment_countries.description: Country of each location that fulfils online orders (one entry per country, not per location).

apps_preferred.description: Returns, tracking or post-purchase apps the client uses or prefers

account_type.description: Legacy (question bank 1.0.0): legacy customer accounts are deprecated since 2026-02-26.

own_operation.description: The wholesale business is run by its own team, with its own targets or P&L.

service.description: Customer service: where a shopper's question lands and who answers it. Nothing here was asked before, so a client running a helpdesk and taking orders by phone was undiscovered scope.

platform.description: Where customer conversations are handled after launch

platform_name.description: The named helpdesk, e.g. Gorgias or Zendesk. Never a person.

contact_form.description: Where the storefront contact form delivers

orders_on_behalf.description: Staff create orders for customers (phone, showroom, wholesale) using draft orders

booking.description: Customers book a slot — an in-store appointment, a virtual consultation, or both. Shopify has no native booking; it is an App Store category.

test_environment.description: Whether this system has a non-production environment Merkle can integrate against before go-live.

extra_theme_designs.description: How many storefronts need a genuinely different design beyond the first — a different layout and page structure, not different content, imagery or translations. Per-market customisation reaches section content and block visibility only, never theme settings and never Liquid templates, so a genuinely different design is a second theme to build, deploy and keep in step. A design-system programme per brand is not this: that is Merkle Arc (rule 11.29).

design_system_per_brand.description: Each customer-facing brand needs its own design system (tokens and components), rather than one design system themed per brand (Q9.2.14). With more than one brand this routes to Merkle Arc (rule 11.29).

bespoke_sections.description: How many bespoke sections or blocks the storefront needs beyond the theme's own — sections that are designed and built rather than configured. A handful is the extended design tier; past the line the offering sells, the work is effectively a full template set and prices as the bespoke tier. Shopify's own ceiling is 25 sections per template.

shop_mini.description: A Shop Mini: a full-screen experience inside Shopify's Shop app, built with the Shop Minis React SDK. Not a headless storefront and not a standalone app — a Mini works only inside Shop.

framework.description: Which front end. Hydrogen is Shopify's own, on the Storefront API and hosted on Oxygen; anything else is a front end Shopify does not build, and with an external CMS it is what takes an engagement to Merkle Arc (11.26).

route.description: Consultant decision after a STOP: larger_engagement = Merkle Enterprise Engagement with a dedicated Discovery Phase (outside the S/M/L offers); arc = Merkle Arc, a separate engagement scoped by the Arc practice and neither quoted nor estimated here. Deciding not to bid is recorded on the outcome ledger, not as a route. Ignored on GO.

triggered.description: True when any STOP item is open.

client_requirement.description: The requirement in the client's own words (quote from the answer)

why_this_level.description: Why this resolution level and not a cheaper one (native → app → theme → custom)

limits.description: Documented limits, plan requirements or licence implications of the chosen resolution

architecture.description: Solution architecture drafted by the solution architect (ADR 0017): every decision, integration and data-model element cites official sources; decisions trace to client answers.

assessment.description: One line per axis of the comparison rubric (ai/engine/rubric.js): the same axes on every option, so they can be compared rather than argued.

why_not.description: Options weighed and not taken, with the reason. Required for the Market topology decision.

impact.description: What this decision changes, per audience. Required for the Market topology decision.

register.description: Delivery risks with likelihood, impact, mitigation and owner, each founded on evidence (question ids or exit rules).

provenance.description: Per-answer provenance keyed by JSON pointer into this document (e.g. "/markets/list").

ai.description: AI and agent-driven commerce: how the store appears to AI shopping assistants and which AI capabilities the merchant uses (Shopify agentic storefronts, Catalog, UCP).

agentic_enrolment.description: Auto-enrol in current and future AI channels, approve each channel, off, or undecided

direct_checkout.description: Whether buyers may complete checkout inside the AI assistant

us_buyers.description: Sells to buyers in the United States (eligibility for some agentic channels)

customer_data_sharing.description: Sharing order customer data with AI channels on direct checkout

catalog_readiness.description: Product data meets Shopify Catalog requirements (title, image, price, published)

catalog_mapping_needed.description: Key product data sits in metafields, metaobjects or product titles and needs catalog mapping

crawler_policy.description: Policy for AI crawlers on the online store (robots.txt)

knowledge_base.description: Wants to control the FAQs AI assistants use to answer questions about the store

own_agent_surface.description: Plans to expose its own agent or MCP surface, or build on UCP

merchant_ai_tools.description: Merchant-facing Shopify AI features in scope

sell_through_agents.description: Wants products found and bought inside AI assistants

terms_owner.description: Who can accept Shopify's supplemental terms for AI channels (role, not a name)

sources.description: HTTPS links to the sources a statement relies on (official Shopify documentation first).

tier.description: How much of a project this gate is. Set for migration, from the source platform: WooCommerce is light, Shopware medium, Magento or a custom platform heavy — the published DACH durations differ by a factor of two. Set for SEO continuity from the size of the redirect estate: standard is a map authored and imported, large is one built from a crawl.
